title: Time to first visit of red foxes and raccoon dogs at 69 camera-monitored raccoon carcasses, Yakumo, Hokkaido, Japan, 2016-2019
creator: Nakashima, Yoshihiro
citation: Nakashima, Y. (2024). Data and code for implementing time-to-detection occupancy model [Dataset]. Dryad. https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.kkwh70sbn
abstract: Raccoon carcasses were placed at least 500 m apart in the Yakumo Study Forest, Hokkaido, Japan, 12-23 a year from 2016 to 2019, and watched by camera traps. The time to the first visit records which scavenger came first, the red fox or the raccoon dog; the first visitor censors the other. The authors fitted a two-species time-to-detection occupancy model to estimate the competition between the two scavengers for carcasses.
samplingProtocol: Raccoon carcasses placed at least 500 m apart in forest, each watched by a camera trap until the first visit of a red fox or raccoon dog or the end of monitoring; 12-23 carcasses a year, 2016-2019 (Hashizume et al. 2023).
closureNote: One survey per station (no occasion); the survey ends when the resource is taken or monitoring stops. Replicated within the survey by the time to detection (ruling 2026-11-06).
geographicCoverage: Yakumo Study Forest, Hokkaido, Japan (no coordinates deposited)
covariateNote: obs_ttd_days: days from placement to the species' first take (y = 1), or to the end of the survey of that resource (y = 0: the other species took it first, or monitoring ended). obs_ttd_censored: 1 where the time is censored (y = 0), 0 where it is the species' detection time.

notShipped.code: the authors' Stan and R code
notShipped.wet_mass: the carcass wet-mass series (279 measurements of 19 carcasses; a measurement of the resource, its carcass ids not keyed to the stations) and gen_seq (a plotting grid)

notes: Time to detection (ruling 2026-11-06): y = 1 for the species that took the resource first; the other species is censored at that time (competing risks), so its obs_ttd_days is the time the survey of that resource ended rather than a fixed survey length. Stations are the 69 carcasses of 2016-2019 pooled (years not deposited per carcass). Censoring is at the end of monitoring or at the time the other scavenger came (one carcass visited first by a crow is censored for both, paper s.2.3.2). The deposit has 38 carcasses first visited by foxes; the paper reports 37. Overlaps the data of Hashizume et al. (2023), which the paper reuses.
